senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. שכך) [to sink,] to forget, discard.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 32b:10-15">Ber. 32ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 49:14">Is. XLIX, 14</cite>) <he>אדם … אתה עזבתני ושְׁכַחְתָּנִי</he> if a man marries a woman after abandoning his first wife, he remembers the doings of his first wife, but thou hast abandoned me and also forgotten me.

<cite ref="Isaiah 49:14">Ib.</cite> <he>כלום אֶשְׁכַּח עולות וכ׳</he> will I ever forget the burnt-offerings of rams and the first born that thou didst offer &c.? <cite ref="Isaiah 49:14">Ib.</cite> <he>שמא תִשְׁכַּח … סיני</he> wilt thou forget what I did at Sinai? <cite ref="Mishnah Peah 5:7">Peah V, 7</cite> <he>העומר ששְׁכָחוּהוּ … ולא ש׳ וכ׳</he> a sheaf which the laborers overlooked in collecting, but the employer had not overlooked.
<cite ref="Mishnah Peah 7:1">Ib. VII, 1</cite> <he>ושְׁכָחוֹ</he> and he forgot it (left it on the tree).
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 3:8">Ab. III, 8</cite> <he>כל השׁוֹכֵחַ וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="M02941"><he>מִשְׁנָה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Middot 2:5">Midd. II, 5</cite> <he>שָׁכַחְתִּי מה וכ׳</he> I forgot what purpose it served; <cite ref="Yoma 16a:3">Yoma 16ᵃ</cite>; a. v. fr.—Part. pass. <he>שָׁכוּחַ</he>; f. <cite ref="U01133"><he>שְׁכוּחָה</he></cite>,
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:1:2">Y. Sabb. VI, 7ᵈ</cite> <he>והיא ש׳</he> and she may forget herself, v. <cite ref="U00694"><he>שַׁחֲצָנִית</he></cite>.—
senses.label: a

units: <cite ref="Bava Metzia 11a:10">B. Mets. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>ש׳ מעיקרו</he> a sheaf forgotten at the start (overlooked in collecting); <he>זכור ולבסוף ש׳</he>, v. <cite ref="G00467"><he>זָכַר</he></cite>. Ber. l. c. (ref. to Is. l. c.) <he>היינו עזובה היינו ש׳</he> is not abandoned the same as forgotten? (Ms. O. <he>עֲזִיבָה … שְׁכִיחָה …</he>).
senses.label: b

senses.gloss: <cite ref="U01136">same</cite>. Y. Ber. V, 9ᵃ top <he>לא במהרה הוא מְשַׁכֵּחַ</he> will not easily forget it.
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 99a:12-22">Snh. 99ᵃ</cite> <he>כל … ומְשַׁכְּחָהּ וכ׳</he> he who studied the Law and neglects it (fails to review it) is like a woman that gives birth and buries; a. e.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 2:2">Ab. II, 2</cite> <he>שיגיעת … מְשַׁכַּחַת עון</he> (or <he>מַשְׁכַּחַת</he>) the employment of the mind in both of them causes man to forget sin.

<cite ref="Tosefta Sotah 3:12">Tosef. Sot. III, 12</cite> <he>אתם מְשַׁכְּחִין … אני אֲשַׁכֵּחַ וכ׳</he> you make the law of free trade forgotten among you, I will cause you to be forgotten in the world; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 109a">Snh. 109ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>באו ונְשַׁכֵּחַ וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="T00204"><he>רֶגֶל</he></cite>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Beitzah 15b:4">Bets. 15ᵇ</cite> <he>להַשְׁכִּיחוֹ</he>, v. <cite ref="G00467"><he>זָכַר</he></cite>. Ab. l. c., v. supra; a. e.

<cite ref="Temurah 14b:16">Tem. 14ᵇ</cite> <he>מוטב … ואל תִּשְׁתַּכֵּחַ וכ׳</he> (some ed. <he>תִּשָּׁבֵחַ</he>) it is better that a law be uprooted (disregarded) than that the Law be forgotten in Israel.
<cite ref="Temurah 15b:37">Ib. 15ᵇ</cite> <he>שלשה … נִשְׁתַּכְּחוּ וכ׳</he> three thousand traditional rules were forgotten during the days of mourning for Moses.
<cite ref="Temurah 16a:16">Ib. 16ᵃ</cite> <he>אף … נִשְׁתַּכְּחָה וכ׳</he> also the rule concerning a sin offering whose owner died (before it was brought) was forgotten during &c.
<cite ref="Temurah 16a:63">Ib.</cite> <he>שלא יִשְׁתַּכֵּחַ … מלבי</he> that what I have learned be not forgotten out of my mind.
<cite ref="Pesachim 54b:3">Pes. 54ᵇ</cite> <he>על המת שישתכח מן הלב</he> that the dead should be forgotten out of mind; a. fr.
